description:
23. **A CARD RETIRED BY NARROWING GETS FLAGGED AND REPORTED.** Ruled by Marc after two rounds:
    first "tag it", which turned out to be unbuildable, then "flag it".

    **Why a tag cannot do it.** Anki tags live on NOTES; suspension and flags live on CARDS. The
    tool's own algebra shows the split — `addTags` takes note ids, `suspend` takes card ids.
    Narrowing retires ONE card of a note whose siblings are healthy, so a note-level tag would mark
    all of them and every report would call the whole note parked.

    **Why a flag rather than suspension.** The settled ruling is that the tool cannot tell its own
    suspension from Marc's, which is exactly why an orphan carries a tag ALONGSIDE its suspension —
    the tag is the record. For a single card there is no tag available, so suspension alone would
    leave the tool unable to recognise its own work and unable to undo it safely when the marker is
    widened again. A flag is per-card AND self-identifying: it does both jobs. The counter-argument
    for suspension — that a flag does not remove the card from review — is void, because a retired
    card's front renders empty and Anki never queues it.

    **Colour 7**, all seven being free in the live collection today.

    **What is still to build:** the tool must work out which ordinals a spec calls for, compare
    that against the note's current gate field values — available in `ObservedNote.fields`, which
    is fetched on every run and consumed by NOTHING today — flag the difference, un-flag on
    widening, and say so in the report.

    **Cloze is out of scope and must say so.** A cloze note's card count comes from its CONTENT,
    not from gate fields, so "which ordinals should exist" is not answerable the same way. Retiring
    a cloze deletion is the separate, still-open ordinal-drift problem.

    **One correspondence needs pinning by a test.** `{{^ValueOnly}}` and `{{#ThreeWay}}` OPEN their
    front templates and wrap them entirely, which is what makes them card gates; `{{#Context}}` and
    `{{#ConceptLabel}}` sit inside wrapping display fragments and are not. That distinction lives
    only in the template text today, so a template edit could silently change which cards exist —
    and this feature would then flag the wrong card.
design:
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE PREMISE OF THE FLAG-OVER-SUSPEND RULING IS FALSE. REPORTED BY MARC 2026-09-01.
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The description above dismisses suspension with one sentence: "The counter-argument for suspension
— that a flag does not remove the card from review — is void, because a retired card's front
renders empty and ANKI NEVER QUEUES IT."

Marc, from using the collection: "anki show me many empty cards in my review (and the danger
'delete', deletes the note, not just the empty card)".

So Anki DOES queue them. The counter-argument is not void; it is correct. A flag does not remove a
card from review, and the card is shown. The ruling chose flag over suspension on the strength of a
claim that does not hold, and the consequence is live in Marc's collection today.

THE SECOND HALF IS WORSE THAN THE FIRST. The obvious remedy in the reviewer — Delete — removes the
NOTE, not the card. A note retired by narrowing has healthy siblings carrying real review history,
and deleting the note destroys them. So the user is shown a blank card, and the one action the
interface offers destroys data the tool spent its whole design protecting.

WHERE THE FALSE CLAIM CAME FROM. `docs/findings/ANKICONNECT-BEHAVIOUR.md` states it and says
plainly that it is UNVERIFIED: "no test established whether it is actually presented in a review
session… That sentence is load-bearing and is currently in doubt." Traced further back, the
retired markdown tracker asserted it with no citation, and this bead's description is a
byte-identical copy of that assertion rather than a second witness. A hedge was dropped in the
copy, and the flat version then decided a design.

WHAT THIS REOPENS. The flag-versus-suspend choice, at least. Two of the ruling's three arguments
survive — a tag cannot do it, because tags are per-note and this retires one card of a healthy
note; and a flag is self-identifying where suspension is not, so the tool can recognise and undo
its own work. Neither argues against doing BOTH. The likely shape is flag AND suspend: the flag is
the record, the suspension is what stops Marc meeting a blank card. That needs Marc's ruling rather
than an assistant's inference, and it is not made here.

ALSO WORTH ESTABLISHING, and cheap: whether the empty cards Marc is seeing come from this tool's
note types or from elsewhere in the collection. Either way the premise is falsified — it is a claim
about what Anki does — but it decides whether this is a live defect in the tool's own output or a
hazard it must design around.
title: Flag and report a card retired by narrowing

description:
**OBSERVATION.** `extract/Tables.scala:207` reads the concept label from the FIRST header cell —
`headerRow.headOption.map(display.text).getOrElse("")` — and nothing anywhere validates that cell.
The refusal gate at `:220` is `descriptorColumns.forall(_.segment.isEmpty)`, and
`descriptorColumns` is `headerRow.drop(1)`. So a table whose first header cell is BLANK, but which
has at least one usable descriptor column, passes the gate and emits pair cards carrying
`ConceptLabel == ""`.

**WHY THAT IS A DEFECT ON ITS OWN TERMS.** `ConceptLabel` exists precisely to stop a card asking
"Frontal WHAT?" — its own docstring says the first column header "names what the rows ARE — `Bone`
over `Frontal`, `Parietal` — so without it a card asks 'anterior border: orbital rim' and expects
'Frontal' while never saying it wants the name of a bone." A blank first header reproduces exactly
the defect the field was introduced to prevent, silently and legally.

The remedy is presumably a refusal beside the existing `SpecError.TableWithoutDescriptors`, whose
message pattern ("give the column a heading") already fits.

**A SECOND CONSEQUENCE, WHICH IS HOW IT WAS FOUND.** `ConceptLabel` is empty by construction on a
HEADING concept-descriptor card (`Extractor`'s three-field arm sets it to `""` explicitly) and
non-empty on a TABLE pair card. That difference was silently doing load-bearing work: it is what
stops a table-origin note being mistaken for a heading-origin one. Blank the first header and that
discriminator evaporates.

Worked case: Anki holds a stranded pair card `Concept="Postgres"`, `Descriptor="Consistency"`,
`Description="all reads see the latest write"`, `ConceptLabel=""`. The vault holds a heading card
`## Databases / ### Consistency` with the same body. They become byte-indistinguishable.

**HOW IT WAS FOUND, 2026-09-04.** Three agents independently built move-detection mechanisms
(`oas-ugc`), then argued their differences directly with each other. The blank-header hole was
found by one of them while attacking another's design, and confirmed by a second against the
source. Verified independently from the main session: the gate reads only `headerRow.drop(1)`, and
`headerRow.headOption` appears at `:207` and `:212` and nowhere else.

**ALL THREE MOVE-DETECTION DESIGNS FALSELY PAIR THE WORKED CASE ABOVE**, and one of the agents
checked whether the design the three converged on closes it. **IT DOES NOT** — the blank header is
what makes the marker-gate fields agree, so the admission floor holds and the pairing is offered
with only a divergence line to warn a reader. Flagged here rather than left implied: the fix
belongs at extraction, not in move detection.

**RELATED.** `oas-ugc` (a moved heading loses its review history) is where the move-detection work
is recorded. This bug is independent of it and worth fixing whatever happens there — closing it
restores `ConceptLabel` as a reliable discriminator for whichever design ships.
title: A table with a blank first header cell is accepted, and its cards cannot say what they are about

description:
A cloze deletion that spans a soft line break silently makes no card. Red marrow sits in ==<<1|spongy>>== bone; the ==<<2|medullary cavity>>== holds yellow marrow instead. ^marrow-sites The first deletion becomes {{c1::spongy}}. The second does not become a cloze at all: it renders into the card as the literal text `==<<2|medullary
cavity>>==`. No refusal, no warning, no missing-card report. The author sees a card and assumes both gaps are in it. FOUND 2026-08-31 while adding a block-cloze fixture to dummy-vault. The golden's rendered field is what exposed it; nothing else would have. THE CAUSE IS DELIBERATE, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A DECISION AND NOT A REPAIR. parser/ObsidianSyntax.scala:344 reads `delimitedBy("==").failOn('\n')`. That is the dialect-wide pattern - embeds (:230), wikilinks (:245) and inline maths (:301) all do it - and the reason is recorded once, on the wikilink parser at :236: an unclosed delimiter degrades to plain text rather than running away and swallowing the rest of the document. Sound, and not written on the highlight parser. WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY CORRECT. docs/design/CLOZE-REDESIGN.md:101-102 rules the opposite principle for the same construct: "Inside a paragraph a line break is soft wrap, an artifact of how the file happens to be wrapped." That argument was made to reject scoping a card to a LINE. The highlight parser then makes the same artifact decide whether a card exists, and does it in silence - which is the failure mode model/CardSpec.scala:137-157 names as "silent success, this project's signature failure". WHO HITS IT. Anyone whose editor or formatter wraps prose at a column width, which is how most of this repository's own markdown is written. Prettier and most web clippers do it. The author cannot see the difference on the rendered page in Obsidian, where the highlight spans the wrap and looks correct. PRECEDENT FOR ALLOWING IT. Display maths already opts out of failOn('\n') deliberately - parser/ObsidianSyntax.test.scala:555: "really does have to cross those newlines. That is why display maths does not fail on one." So the mechanism exists and has been used once with a reason. UNTESTED EITHER WAY. No test asserts what a highlight spanning a newline does.
design:
THREE CANDIDATES, NONE CHOSEN.

1. LET A HIGHLIGHT CROSS A NEWLINE, as display maths already does. Matches the ruling that
   a line break is a wrapping artifact, and matches what Obsidian renders. Cost: an
   unclosed `==` can then run past the end of its paragraph, which is the hazard
   failOn('\n') exists to bound. Needs a bound of its own - a blank line, or the end of the
   block - rather than no bound.

2. KEEP THE CONSTRAINT AND REFUSE LOUDLY. A `==<<` with no closing `>>==` before the line
   ends is almost certainly a wrapped cloze rather than prose about syntax, so name it the
   way BuildFailure.ClozeBlockUnanchored names a missing anchor. Cheapest, and turns a
   silent omission into a message. Cost: a false refusal for anyone genuinely writing
   `==<<` in prose about this tool - this repository's own documentation does.

3. KEEP IT AND DOCUMENT IT. Cheapest of all and the weakest: it leaves the author to
   discover the rule by losing a card, which is what happened here.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: what Obsidian itself renders for a highlight spanning a soft wrap. If
Obsidian shows one continuous highlight, this tool diverges from its own source format
while claiming to model it, and (1) becomes much harder to argue against.
title: A cloze deletion spanning a soft line break silently makes no card

VERIFIED against the code 2026-08-30. isCloze is declared in every manifest, sent on createModel, and read live by the retype gate — and driftBetween compares only fields, template names and styling. So a note type whose kind differs from what the repository declares passes the drift check silently, and the retype gate then reasons from a property nothing has confirmed.

The design that found this argued it must be its OWN drift case, marked UNREPAIRABLE, because no AnkiConnect action changes a model's kind. That matters for wording rather than for detection: InstallOutcome.isClean goes false on any drift, so an unrepairable case becomes standing noise on every run unless its message says plainly that the tool cannot repair it and what it means for the retype gate.

It also needs the live collection's actual kinds read first — Obsidian Cloze carrying MODEL_CLOZE and Obsidian Cloze Sequence carrying MODEL_STD were read once on 2026-08-21 and never re-checked. If that reading was wrong, adding the check makes install-note-types permanently non-clean with no repair path.

description:
40. **A LEGACY NOTE IS READ FOREVER INSTEAD OF BEING MIGRATED ONCE.** Ruled by Marc 2026-08-29.
    **Nothing is built.**

    **The settled principle.** Notes generated from the Obsidian vault do NOT use Anki's stock
    note types. The tool is ruled never to write to a note type it did not create (2026-08-21),
    it owns five, and all five declare `Identity`. **So every note it generates carries the
    field, by construction rather than by luck.**

    **Which makes a note without the field exactly one thing: a LEGACY note** — written before
    the field existed, when the tool wrote to stock `Basic` and `Cloze`. Its identity is in a tag
    because that was the only home available at the time.

    **WHAT IS WRONG TODAY.** Such a note is READ through its tag on every run, indefinitely, and
    nothing ever moves it. The tag reader is treated as a second permanent home rather than as
    the means of ending the state it serves. Marc's question — *why limit and contort ourselves
    with Anki's stock things?* — is the correction: nothing needs accommodating that can be
    fixed.

    **WHAT SHOULD HAPPEN.** A run that finds a note on a note type this tool does not own should
    MIGRATE it onto the owned type its marker asks for, and say so — the same way a note-type
    move is already reported. Moving stock `Basic` onto `Obsidian Basic` is not a shrink, so no
    gate refuses it, and the retype machinery already exists.

    **WHAT THAT RETIRES, once no collection holds one:** the tag half of `CardSearch`'s two
    searches, `Executor.resolveFromTag`, the add-on's tag branch in `core.py`, and the test in
    `CardSearch.test.scala` that guards both halves. Each of those now points here.

    **WHY IT CANNOT SIMPLY BE DELETED NOW**, which is the trap this item exists to keep shut.
    Removing the tag reader before the notes are migrated strands exactly the notes it exists to
    rescue, and does so INVISIBLY: their cards stop appearing in Anki, and an empty Browse window
    reads as *this note made no cards* rather than as a fault. The end condition is a judgement
    somebody makes about the collections in the world, not a state the code can detect alone.

    **TWO WRONG STATEMENTS WERE WITHDRAWN GETTING HERE, both Claude's, both recorded at the sites
    so neither is re-proposed.** The first said the tag half "goes when the tag does", which
    invited deleting it on a schedule nothing tracked. The second overcorrected to "permanently,
    not transitionally", which invites building on two homes and asking which is authoritative.
    Neither is true; the reader is migration machinery with an end.

    _Marc also caught the method: asked why the design should contort around stock note types,
    Claude reached for a measurement of what his collection currently holds. That answers "does
    this bite today", not "what should the design be" — the same status-quo-for-status-bono error
    recorded in `docs/design/CLOZE-REDESIGN.md`'s header. The principled answer needed no measurement._

description:
Pressing `e` on a card in the Anki reviewer opens Anki's own editor instead of the source note in
Obsidian. Reported by Marc 2026-08-31. The feature shipped before 2026-08-27 and was in daily use.

WHAT THE ADD-ON DOES WITH THAT KEYPRESS. `addon/obsidian_edit/core.py` returns one of three
verdicts. `Open` sends the person to Obsidian. `Explain` says why it could not and ALSO opens
Anki's editor. `NotOurs` — no identity found on the note — opens Anki's editor SILENTLY, on the
reasoning at core.py:52 that a keypress doing nothing is indistinguishable from a broken add-on.

So the symptom Marc describes, Anki's editor with no message, is the `NotOurs` path: the add-on
decided the note is not one of ours. An `Explain` would have printed something.

WHAT IS RULED OUT, checked 2026-08-31:
  - The add-on is not stale. `addons21/obsidian_edit` is a SYMLINK to `addon/obsidian_edit` in
    this repository, so it is always whatever is committed.
  - The field name matches. `core.py:28` has `IDENTITY_FIELD = "Identity"`; `model/Marker.scala`
    declares the same.
  - The legacy path is present: `core.py`'s `identity()` reads the field, then falls back to a
    `src::` tag.
  - The binary exists and runs. `~/.local/bin/obsidian-anki-sync` resolves to `target/`, built
    2026-08-30 09:39.
  - `locate` works. Run against a real vault id it returned a `obsidian://adv-uri` URI and a
    correct diagnosis for an unknown card.
  - Today's commits are not implicated: the installed binary predates all three of them, and
    every other commit since it was built touches only documents and beads.

WHAT IS NOT RULED OUT, and needs the live collection to settle:
  - The note carries neither an `Identity` field nor a `src::` tag. It would then be a note this
    tool did not generate, or one whose identity was lost. Settle by opening the card in Anki's
    browser and looking at its fields and tags.
  - The note is on a note type this tool does not own, so it has no `Identity` field to carry
    one. Settle the same way.
  - The add-on's config is not being read. `meta.json` holds binary, vault_path and java_home;
    `vault_name` is empty, which is legitimate — `locate` falls back to the vault directory's
    name.
design:
THE SILENT FALLBACK IS WHY THIS IS HARD TO DIAGNOSE, and it is worth reconsidering as part of the
fix. `NotOurs` opens Anki's editor and says NOTHING, so a person cannot tell "this note is not
mine" from "the add-on is broken" — which is exactly the confusion this report started as. The
reasoning behind it is sound as far as it goes: the alternative considered was a keypress that
does nothing at all.

But the choice was between silence and nothing. A third option was not considered: open Anki's
editor AND say, once, why Obsidian was not used. `Explain` already does precisely that, so the
mechanism exists and `NotOurs` simply does not use it.

Whatever the cause turns out to be, a person pressing `e` and landing in Anki's editor should be
able to find out why without reading the add-on's source.
notes:
2026-09-02 — THE OBSERVABILITY HALF IS BUILT AND MERGED to main as 3f3991f (branch `kxf-quiet`,
commits 4f5ffba red, 2cc0680 green, e1df713 correction). THE REPORTED FAULT IS NOT DIAGNOSED. This
work makes it diagnosable; it does not explain it.

WHAT CHANGED. The `NotOurs` verdict used to mean "no `src::` tag" and delegated in silence. It now
means "no `Identity` field at all" — a note type this tool does not own — and still delegates in
silence, which is correct for nearly every note in a real collection. A note that HAS the field
with nothing in it now yields `Explain` instead, so a card that is OURS and broken says why.
No new verdict was added: `Explain` already meant "no URI could be produced, say why and still
open Anki's editor". The shell had simply routed this case into the wrong arm.

RULED AGAINST ON THE WAY, and recorded because it will occur to someone again: a first attempt
gave `NotOurs` a reason and spoke on EVERY identity-less note. Marc rejected it — most cards in a
collection are genuinely Anki-made, pressing Edit on one SHOULD open Anki's editor with nothing
said, and a message there is noise on the majority to serve the rare case. That rejection also
dissolved two design questions the first attempt had raised (whether to check note-type NAMES,
which would have created an unchecked second copy of the five names; and an eroded guarantee on
the delegation path, which no longer has anything on it).

A FALSE REPAIR WAS CAUGHT IN REVIEW AND WITHDRAWN. The message first ended "Re-syncing the vault
should fill it in." That is false and dangerous: `CardSearch.everythingOwned` is
`"Identity:src::*" or "tag:src::*"`, so a note with an empty field and no tag matches neither half
and the sync cannot see it — and per that file's own comment, a note the search misses reads as a
note that does not exist, which is the input that makes the tool create it again. The message now
states only what was observed and instructs nothing, and a test pins the absence of advice.

THAT REVIEW EXPOSED A SEPARATE DEFECT, filed as oas-x9i: such a note is invisible to the tool
entirely — never enumerated, never counted, never reported, and unreachable by identity-recovery
tiers 1 and 2, which only ever see notes the search returned.

WHAT REMAINS FOR THIS ISSUE, and it is one keypress. Rebuild, `just install`, press `e` on the
card that failed. Either a message names the cause, or silence means the note carries no
`Identity` field at all and is on a note type this tool does not own — which is itself the answer.
Two of the three causes listed above are then distinguished; the third, the add-on's config not
being read, would show as a different message.

KNOWN RESIDUE, deliberate. The message's opening clause asserts the card is on one of this tool's
note types, decided by whether a field named `Identity` exists. A foreign shared deck declaring
such a field would be told the same. Milder than what it replaced — it prompts no action — and the
same field-presence rule is already used tool-wide at `plan/Planner.scala:571-574`, so narrowing it
here alone would make the add-on stricter than the tool it serves.
title: Pressing e in Anki opens Anki's editor instead of the note in Obsidian

12. **`prune`** — deletes flagged cards after the list has been reviewed. Named in `README.md`

description:
The family in docs/findings/PARSER-DISAGREEMENTS.md has six rows, and those six are what has been tripped over rather than the result of looking. Every time anybody has looked it has gained a member, which is an argument that the list is a sample rather than a census.

A deliberate pass would replace an anecdotal list with a measured one: write each construct Obsidian supports into a throwaway vault, run inspect, and record where the two parsers disagree. Read-only with respect to any real collection.

It bears directly on the open question of whether this earns a subsystem at all. One instance in one vault is an argument for a cheap fix; a measured family is an argument for a check.

description:
19. **THE GIT-REPLAY MEASUREMENT (called M1 in `docs/findings/EVOLVABILITY.md`) HAS NOT BEEN RUN, AND IT
    GATES THE IDENTITY DECISION.** Read-only, no Anki, no writes, roughly an afternoon: walk the
    vault's git history, run the extractor over each pair of trees, diff the key sets, and
    classify every key death — file deleted, file renamed, ancestor heading reworded, marked
    heading reworded, frontmatter `id` changed, body-only edit. Then count how many cards each
    ancestor rewording would have orphaned; **that number is the amplification factor.**

    **Why it is worth an afternoon:** every option for making reformulation affordable is
    currently being weighed on the assumption that heading renames dominate the cost of change.
    Nobody has checked. Renaming is the most VIVID cost, which is not the same as the largest,
    and the answer decides whether the effort belongs on heading renames or on ancestor renames —
    which have a far larger blast radius and no good candidate remedy.

## Method — what the last two days added to "the mistakes worth not repeating"

_Written 2026-08-26. Each of these cost real time on 2026-08-25 and every one is the same shape as
the bugs this project keeps finding in itself: **something that looks like verification and is
not.**_

- **A TEST THAT COMPARES TWO ABSENT THINGS PASSES.** Three separate instances in two days. A new
  parser test asserted "the inline spelling reads the same as the block spelling" and was green
  while BOTH were `None` — it would have stayed green through the entire defect it was written for.
  The measurement of whether unsuspending restores scheduling compared ten card columns and
  reported every one identical; three of them, **including `interval`, the one that matters most**,
  were `None` on both sides, because `cardsInfo` returns `interval` and not `ivl`. **Assert
  presence before asserting agreement, and make the check abort when a field is absent on both
  sides rather than counting it as a match.**

- **A GUARD CAN BE DEAD CODE AND ITS TEST STILL PASS.** `TagCodec.decode` grew a clause refusing a
  path marked as non-heading that names no kind. Deleting the clause killed no test — such a tag is
  ALREADY refused, for a different reason, because its first heading segment is empty. The clause's
  only real product is its MESSAGE. A test asserting `isLeft` could not see that; one asserting the
  reason can. **When a mutation survives, the usual finding is not that the code is unnecessary but
  that the test is measuring the wrong thing.**

- **A DOCSTRING THAT PROMISES A TEST MUST BE WRITTEN WITH THAT TEST, IN THE SAME PASS.** The
  `CardPath.Note` documentation said "a test asserts that nothing produces it yet" before any such
  test existed. That is the same false-comment defect being fixed elsewhere in this file, committed
  fresh. Write the sentence and the assertion together or write neither.

- **A COMPILE ERROR CAN BE A GHOST.** A `match may not be exhaustive` names a case that exists in
  neither the working tree nor `HEAD` — that is a stale incremental-compile artifact from an
  earlier mutation run, not a real error. Check `git grep` before debugging it.

- **PERL WITH `-CSD` DOUBLE-ENCODES LITERAL UTF-8 IN A HEREDOC.** Section signs and em dashes came
  out as mojibake in a committed document. Every doc edit since is done in Python with an explicit
  `encoding="utf-8"` on both the read and the write, and checked with a grep for the mojibake
  bytes afterwards.

- **DELETE BY LOCATING TWO EXACT LITERALS, NEVER BY A REGEX WITH A LAZY MULTILINE WILDCARD.** One
  such regex deleted an entire type: the replacement docstring reused the opening sentence of the
  docstring being removed, so the match started from the wrong occurrence. The `cp` backup made it
  a non-event. Compute the span, assert the start is unique, refuse if the span is an implausible
  number of lines, and print what is about to go.

- **A MUTATION HARNESS THAT COUNTS TEST FAILURES CANNOT SEE A MUTATION THE COMPILER REJECTED.**
  _2026-08-26._ A mutation was reported as SURVIVING when the build had in fact refused it —
  `-Wconf:msg=exhaustive:e` will not accept a match that stops being exhaustive, so there were no
  tests and therefore no failures, which counts identically to zero kills. That is the strongest
  possible outcome being reported as the weakest. **Count compile errors and test failures
  separately**, and treat a mutation that does not build as killed by the compiler.

- **ASSERT THE CONSEQUENCE, NOT THE MESSAGE.** _2026-08-26._ A test named "two schema notes yield
  no vocabulary at all" asserted only that the refusal was REPORTED. Silently adopting the first of
  the two vocabularies left it green, because the report is emitted either way. A test that names a
  behaviour in its title and checks only the diagnostic is the same class of thing as a docstring
  that promises a test: it reads as verification and is not.

- **WHEN A MUTATION SURVIVES, FIND OUT WHICH ARM IS LOAD-BEARING BEFORE BLAMING THE TEST.**
  _2026-08-26._ The usual finding is a weak test. This time it was DEAD CODE: making the
  bare-`Header` arm of the heading predicate throw killed nothing, because Laika's section builder
  wraps every heading in a `Section` and that arm is unreachable through any vault. The arm was
  kept — deleting it would send a bare header to the catch-all and answer "not a heading", so a
  document full of headings would report having none — and the predicate is now driven directly on
  hand-built syntax trees so both arms are covered.

- **A DRIFT-GUARD TEST YOU WROTE YOURSELF IS EVIDENCE YOU CREATED THE DRIFT.** _2026-08-26._ The
  declarations parser had a test asserting its three words agreed with the marker vocabulary. That
  test existed only because the parser had invented a second vocabulary instead of composing the
  first — and the second one clashed, since `1way` on a heading is a two-field card. Composing
  `Marker.parse` deleted the drift, the lookup table, the word list its messages needed, and the
  guard. **Before writing a test that two things agree, ask why they are two things.**

## OPEN — verified by the pipeline brainstorm, 2026-08-26

_Three facts, each checked by running or reading rather than inferred, and each surviving the
adversarial review at `docs/history/PIPELINE-DESIGN-REVIEW.md`. They are lifted out of that 38,000-character
document because a finding nobody can find is a finding nobody acts on._

`docs/design/EDIT-IN-OBSIDIAN.md` says in three places that one number is unmeasured and that the
whole choice hangs on it:

  :208  "C is chosen PROVIDED a native `locate` binary starts fast enough to sit under the `e` key.
         That number has not been measured."
  :237  "UNVERIFIED: the startup time of such a binary has not been measured... this is the single
         number that justifies option C over option A."
  :478  "The one number that decides option C over option A."

RESOLVED BY MARC 2026-09-01, from use rather than from a benchmark: "all i can say... until it
worked... worked nicely, and the latency was totally 'bare-able'."

So the gate was never applied and did not need to be. Option C shipped on the JVM, was used daily,
and the latency was acceptable to the only person it had to be acceptable to. Living with it is
stronger evidence than the benchmark would have been.

The strict fact remains that the NATIVE-IMAGE number was never taken — what
`docs/history/EDIT-IN-OBSIDIAN-PLAN.md:258-270` measured is the JVM assembly, 0.72s median, split
0.30s JVM start and 0.42s vault read. But that measurement makes the question moot rather than
answering it: a native image could only remove the 0.30s and cannot touch the 0.42s, the vault half
is the half that grows, and the build already rejects native-image on stronger grounds than speed
(snakeyaml resolves classes by reflection, so the binary would build and then break on a path only
a live run reaches).

THE EDIT: the three sentences stop saying the number is pending and say the choice was taken and
validated in use, with the vault-half reasoning as why the number stopped mattering. `docs/history/`
cannot be cited for instructions, so the reasoning is carried here rather than pointed at.

true of the moment it was taken. That is only true if the moment is recorded. A latency figure with
no machine, no load, no note about a warm or cold page cache is a sample presented as a constant,

marks. Worth a rule for how this project records a measurement — at minimum what was run, on what,

description:
RULED BY MARC, 2026-09-01, in answer to a direct question about which of four things this is.
Recorded verbatim because every previous retelling of it lost a hedge:

  "a general principle, a philosophy... a bit like mutation in FP ... sometime... for some algos,
   local mutation is fine... so no mutation is the general rule, but not the Sharia nore the holy
   bible. example our review / fix tools for example might have to write...."

SO: A DEFAULT, WITH THE BURDEN OF JUSTIFICATION ON THE EXCEPTION. Not an invariant, and not a
free-for-all. The tool does not write the vault because that is the right default, in the way an
FP codebase does not mutate — and a specific, argued local exception is legitimate rather than
heretical. Review and fix tooling is named as the likely first exception.

WHAT THIS OVERTURNS. The absolute form is stated across the corpus and must come down:
  - `cli/Help.scala:55` prints it to users as an unconditional promise. It is also stale in the
    same sentence (identity is a FIELD, not a tag, since 2026-08-28).
  - `docs/design/EDIT-IN-OBSIDIAN.md:148` — "this repository's central property".
  - `docs/history/HANDOFF.md:11` — "the one design property that everything else serves".
  - `docs/design/CLOZE-REDESIGN.md:51` — "a tool that writes into your vault is a different tool",
    a prohibition with a reason, built from Marc's narrower "I said could we USE ^blockid — not
    should the tool WRITE it".
  - `docs/reference/REQUIREMENTS.md:122` marks the requirement `[derived]`, citing a derivation
    from the learning model that does not exist there.

WHAT IT DOES NOT OVERTURN. The block-anchor design still stands; only its justification changes.
"The tool CANNOT write it" becomes "the tool does not write it by default, Obsidian generates one
with a keystroke, and no exception has been argued for" — which is a live argument rather than an
appeal to an invariant. Anyone wanting the tool to write anchors now has a door: argue the
exception.

THE WARNING THAT SAW THIS COMING, and was filed and ignored. `docs/findings/EVOLVABILITY.md:369`,
dated 2026-08-25: the premise "conflates a structural invariant with a design choice, and the
choice is currently riding on the invariant's reputation." Six days later the choice was printed
in `--help`. Worth keeping as the corpus's best evidence that a hedge does not survive retelling.
title: The tool does not write the vault: a default with justified exceptions, not an invariant

description:
**OBSERVATION.** The gate that decides whether a note may be moved from one note type to another
reads its facts from the LIVE COLLECTION. The action it admits writes content built from the
REPOSITORY'S DECLARATION. While those two disagree about a note type, the verdict comes from one
source and the content from the other, and nothing compares them.

**WHERE, read from the code 2026-09-02.** `plan/Retyping.scala:396` — `shapesOf` reads
`anki.noteTypeIsCloze(name)` for both types, and `judgeShapes` compares live against live. That
much is sound: the gate exists to answer whether a card's ordinal means a template index or a
cloze number, and it answers it from the collection.

The `SyncAction.Retype` it admits is built at `plan/Planner.scala:380`, where `to` is
`sourced.spec.noteTypeName` and `fields` is `sourced.spec.fields` — both from the vault marker,
i.e. from the repository's model of the target type.

**THE FAILURE, CONCRETELY.** Suppose `Obsidian Cloze` stood in the collection as STANDARD while
the repository declares it cloze. The gate reads two live-standard types with one template each,
judges the move admissible — and it IS admissible by that test. The tool then writes the note as
the repository's cloze type, putting `{{c1::…}}` markup into a standard note type. Anki stores it
verbatim and generates one card with the braces showing. No error on write, no error on read.

**LATENT, NOT ACTIVE.** All five note types were measured against the live collection on
2026-09-02 and are correct. The precondition does not hold today.

**HOW IT WAS FOUND.** While building the cloze-kind drift check (`oas-ksv`, closed 2026-09-03).
That item's own premise said the retype gate "reasons from a property nothing has confirmed";
checking it showed the premise was wrong in mechanism and the truth was worse — the gate's verdict
is fine, and the hole is one level over, in what the admitted action writes.

**WHY IT IS NOT CLOSED BY `oas-ksv`.** That change makes a kind mismatch visible: an install run
now reports it and refuses to repair it. So the precondition would be caught and reported before a
retype could act on it. But "caught first by something else" is a property of today's code, not a
guarantee, and it is exactly the reasoning that leaves a hazard undocumented until the thing
catching it moves.

---

**SUGGESTIONS, not a choice.**

- Compare the declaration against the live collection inside the gate, so the verdict and the
  content are answered from the same source.
- Or widen `NoteTypeInstaller.readiness` so a kind mismatch refuses a `sync` outright rather than
  only an install. The agent that found this declined to do that unprompted: it changes what a run
  refuses for the author, and `readiness` is the cheap preflight that a per-type
  `findModelsByName` would make materially more expensive.
- Or record the coupling and rely on the install-time check, having stated that reliance.

**CAUTION BEFORE ANY OF THEM.** This is the machinery that moves a note between types, and
`oas-02y` records that its real path has never executed once — every test of it runs against an
in-memory double. Changing it before it has been exercised for real is its own risk, and `oas-02y`
should probably come first.
title: A retype is judged from the collection and written from the declaration

description:
**RAISED BY MARC 2026-09-04**, in his words:

> I have an H2 that is a flashcard. I change the structure of my Obsidian note — make that H2 now
> an H3 under some other H2. The connection is lost. It re-creates the note and cards anew in
> Anki, losing the review history.
>
> Another example: I should be able to move my H2 flashcard from one Obsidian note to another. It
> should be detected. If non-ambiguous, simple re-assignment. If ambiguous, requires manual
> reconciliation — the review tool we're missing.

**WHAT HAPPENS TODAY, verified by execution rather than reading** — two of the three agents below
ran the real `Planner` against `InMemoryAnki` over a vault before and after a re-parenting, and
the second run's plan is exactly `Create(newKey)` and `Flag(oldKey)`, with nothing pairing them.
The old note is tagged and SUSPENDED; a fresh note is created with no history. The history is not
destroyed — it is stranded on the suspended orphan — and nothing reconnects them.

**WHY THE EXISTING RECOVERY NEVER FIRES.** `identityErrorFor` is reached only for
`IdentityProblem.Unreadable` and `Ambiguous` — a broken identity STRING. A moved heading leaves a
perfectly readable identity pointing at a path the vault no longer produces, so that code is never
entered. And `contentHash` includes `Context`, the breadcrumb, which is exactly what a move
changes — so the one hash the tool has is destroyed by the event it would need to witness.

---

## THREE INDEPENDENT IMPLEMENTATIONS EXIST, NONE MERGED

Three agents were given the problem, the house standards and five verified facts about the code —
but deliberately NOT a design — and worked in isolated worktrees without seeing each other. Test
counts below were verified from the main session by re-running each suite, not taken from reports.

    branch move-a  red a10cf4a  green 4c33b00  1063 tests, 0 failed  · 2 new files, nothing else
    branch move-b  red e571f6f  green 723ecca  1068 tests, 0 failed  · 2 new files, nothing else
    branch move-c  red 1aaf633  green 73703d7  1069 tests, 0 failed  · also refactors Planner

All three are REPORT-ONLY by instruction: no `SyncAction`, no execution path, no Anki call of any
kind. Nothing consumes what they produce.

## WHAT ALL THREE CONVERGED ON, WITHOUT COMMUNICATING

- The `sha::` tag is STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE, not merely weak — it hashes `Context`, so a moved
  card's stored hash can never equal the hash of the card the vault now produces. All three
  rejected it independently in those terms.
- The mechanism is DIRECT FIELD COMPARISON, excluding `Identity` (it is the question, and is
  unique by construction) and `Context` (it is the position).
- Pairing is by MUTUAL UNIQUENESS — one candidate each way, or say nothing.
- The vocabulary is "corroborated", never "moved". All three reached for `spike/RenameEvidence.scala`'s
  existing discipline.
- NO threshold, distance or proportion anywhere. Exact byte agreement or nothing.
- All three flagged THE SAME UNVERIFIED PREMISE (see below).
- All three report that the auto-apply question needs no answer from the mechanism.

## WHERE THEY DIVERGE — the fork worth ruling on

**The `Concept` field.** On a heading concept-descriptor card it is the nearest ancestor heading
(`Extractor.scala:74`, `ancestorTitles.lastOption.getOrElse(fileName)`); on a TABLE card it is the
row's first cell. So it is positional in one case and content in the other.

  - **A** excuses it, restricted to `SourceKind.Heading`, as a third weaker grade.
  - **B REFUSES**, with a concrete counterexample: table rows `Kafka | at-least-once` and
    `NATS | at-least-once`. Delete one, add the other, and A's rule reports "kafka/delivery became
    nats/delivery" with confidence — a plausible wrong answer, the stated enemy. B pays for
    refusing: a moved cdd heading card grades one rung weaker.
  - **C sidesteps it** by comparing the KEY's anchor segment rather than the rendered breadcrumb,
    arguing key segments are canonicalised so re-casing an ancestor cannot move them.

B's counterexample looks decisive against A's version.

**Scope of change.** A and B added two files and touched nothing. C additionally refactored the
planner's "has the vault stopped claiming this key?" predicate into a shared `VaultAccounting`,
arguing that restating that rule in a second place is how two answers to one question diverge —
and that this is the question whose wrong answer suspends live cards. Its moved comments were
verified present verbatim in the new location.

## TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS REPOSITORY'S OWN DOCUMENTS, each found independently twice

- `EVOLVABILITY.md` §4A proposes confining candidate search to one frontmatter `id`. Both B and C
  reject it: it makes Marc's second example — a heading moved BETWEEN notes — undetectable by
  construction. B adds that it is not even the conservative choice, because uniqueness across the
  whole vault excludes strictly MORE candidates than uniqueness within one note, so the wide
  search is simultaneously more sensitive and safer.
- The main session told the agents that every note type has exactly one positional field,
  `Context`. That is WRONG, as A found: `Concept` is location-derived too. And `Context` is wider
  than stated — `folders ++ fileName ++ ancestorTitles :+ title` — so moving or renaming the FILE
  also moves it, an event that re-keys nothing.

## THE UNVERIFIED PREMISE ALL THREE DEPEND ON

Every other comparison in this tool is vault-derived on both sides. These are not: they read
`ObservedNote.fields` — what Anki actually holds — and require byte-identity with what
`CardSpec.fields` produces now. **Nobody has measured whether a field round-trips through Anki
unchanged**, and no agent could, because measuring it means writing to a collection.

If Anki normalises field HTML on that path, every one of these mechanisms silently detects nothing
while its whole suite stays green. That is a false negative — the safe direction — but it is a
mechanism that does nothing. Partial evidence exists: the equation probe of 2026-09-04 round-
tripped a field containing backslashes, braces and colons byte-identically, but that field carried
no HTML, and HTML is where an editor is most likely to reformat.

**Settling it is one write and one read on a throwaway profile.** It should happen before any of
these branches is merged.

## RELATED

`oas-6d5` (relink — the ACTION, which needs a human to choose a target) is what this evidence
would turn from a manual hunt into a confirmation. `oas-8q6` (count how many parked orphans are
recoverable renames) is the measurement that says whether this is urgent or theoretical, and it
needs the live collection. `oas-4ti` records Marc's 2026-08-29 ruling that identity stays a PURE
FUNCTION OF THE VAULT, which every design here respects: the hash never becomes a second identity,
it only decides which existing Anki note should be given a key the vault already computed.
notes: ADDENDUM 3 — THE TWO DEFECTS ABOVE LAND ON ONE ROW. A's projection table row 'Descriptor / Front / Title -> segs[-1]' is wrong in TWO INDEPENDENT WAYS, found by different agents: a table row card's Front is Html.rowTable(...) rather than the last segment (B, Tables.scala:397 keys it deeper(base, rowSeg) so segs[-1] is the row concept), and a whole-note card's Front or Title is the file name against an empty segment vector (C, Extractor.fromWholeNote). Neither is a correctness hole alone — the first is caught because Back is substance and fails the floor first, the second is narrow — but the row asserts something untrue about two card shapes, so it wants rewriting rather than patching. That is the defect class all three agents confessed to in their own docstrings this week: a table or docstring claiming more than the code does.
title: A moved heading loses its review history, and nothing detects the move

description:
29. ⚠️ **THE TOOL MUST NOT FORBID A NOTE-TYPE SHRINK. IT MUST STATE THE COST AND LET THE AUTHOR
    DECIDE.** Ruled by Marc 2026-08-27, after the same refusal blocked him twice in one session.
    **Nothing is built.** The full reasoning, including the weaker proposal that was rejected on
    the way to this one, is `docs/design/REVIEW-QUEUE.md` § *Three stances on a refusal*.

    **The ruling in one line.** Changing your mind about your own cards is the AUTHOR's decision,
    made knowingly — not a privilege the tool grants once it judges the stakes low enough.

    **THE REJECTED PROPOSAL IS THE INSTRUCTIVE PART.** Claude proposed making the gate
    evidence-based: refuse a shrink only when the cards actually hold reviews. It is a strictly
    better rule than today's, it unblocks the common case, and **Marc rejected it** — because it
    keeps the tool FORBIDDING and merely moves the threshold. The general form is worth carrying
    to every other gate in this codebase: **when a tool refuses, the question is not only "is the
    threshold right?" but "who is entitled to decide?" — and tuning a threshold answers the first
    while silently keeping the second.**

    **WHY IT CANNOT SIMPLY BE SWITCHED ON, and this is the whole of the remaining work.** The tool
    cannot state the cost because nobody has established it; the refusal's own text admits as much.
    An "apply anyway" meaning *"proceed, and I cannot tell you what happens"* would be WORSE than
    today's refusal, not better — it violates `REVIEW-QUEUE.md`'s founding rule that nothing is
    applied without its cost shown, and it fails in the worse direction because it LOOKS informed.

    **So the sequence is fixed, and M4 is the critical path:**
    1. Run **M4's shrinking half** (`docs/findings/EVOLVABILITY.md`) — an hour in a throwaway profile.
       `Check Database` afterwards is not optional: *orphaned* and *destroyed* look identical
       without it.
    2. Build the third state — *apply anyway, with the cost shown* — which is
       `REVIEW-QUEUE.md`'s row 2 and has never existed.
    3. Only then is the refusal gone rather than relocated.

    **MEASURED 2026-08-27, and it is why this outranks item 28.** `Database Scaleability.md` had
    both headings turned down from `cdd/3way` to `2way`. The tool read the vault correctly —
    `inspect` reports `Obsidian Basic (and reversed card)` for both — and refused the move twice,
    under `SOME ACTIONS FAILED`. **The six cards it protected hold 0 reviews, 0 lapses and 0
    interval between them.** Item 28 is a feature Marc WANTS; this is a defect that STOPS him.

    _Three presentation defects were identified in the same output and are NOT covered by the
    ruling above, because fixing them would not unblock anything — they are worth their own entry

34. **A HYGIENE LINTER FOR SKIPPED HEADING LEVELS.** Ruled desirable by Marc 2026-08-27, parked
    by him 2026-08-28 after the justification originally offered for it turned out to be wrong.
    **Nothing is built.**

    **What it would report.** A heading that jumps more than one level below its parent — `##`
    followed directly by `####` — anywhere in the vault.

    **WHY IT IS NOT URGENT, AND THIS IS THE CORRECTION.** It was filed under item 28 on the claim
    that a skipped level makes "direct child" ambiguous for `#flashcard/sequence/headers`. That
    claim was Claude's and it was wrong. **Laika nests every heading inside the nearest SHALLOWER
    one**, so a `####` under a `##` is a direct child of that `##`, with no ambiguity to resolve —
    and **Obsidian's own outline pane nests it identically**, so the card and the editor agree.
    Nothing this feature does is affected.

    **WHY IT IS STILL WANTED — Marc, 2026-08-28.** Laika's behaviour is helpful and probably what
    anyone would want; the concern is not that it is wrong but that it is *forgiving*. A document
    whose levels drift stays readable while quietly diverging from what its author believes it
    says, and an occasional lint-and-tidy pass is cheap insurance against that surfacing later as
    something surprising.

    **IT IS AN OPTION, NOT A GATE — ruled by Marc.** It must not refuse a sync. A rule that
    refuses notes needs a defect to point at, and this one has none to offer.

    **MEASURED 2026-08-27:** 23 notes in the live vault, **zero** skipped levels. So it would
    report nothing today, and building it later costs no more than building it now — which is
    what makes parking it safe rather than merely convenient.

description:
**OBSERVATION.** A note that sits on one of the five note types this tool owns, whose `Identity`
field is present but EMPTY, and which carries no legacy `src::` tag, is never enumerated by the
tool at all. It is not counted, not reported as a failure, and cannot reach the identity-recovery
machinery that exists for damaged identities.

**THE MECHANISM, read from the code 2026-09-02.** The collection is enumerated exactly once, at
`anki/AnkiConnectClient.scala:204`, which issues `findNotes` with `CardSearch.everythingOwned`.
That search is `model/CardSearch.scala:33`:

    "Identity:src::*" or "tag:src::*"

Both halves require an identity to be PRESENT somewhere. An empty `Identity` field does not match
the first; an absent tag does not match the second. The note is therefore never returned, and
every downstream stage operates on what that search returned.

**WHY THIS IS NOT THE SAME AS AN UNREADABLE IDENTITY, which IS handled.** A note whose identity is
garbled — `Identity: "src::nonsense"`, say — still matches `src::*`, so it comes back, reaches
`plan/Executor.scala:182`, and becomes `IdentityProblem.Unreadable`. Recovery tiers 1 and 2 then
try to rebind it by exact content hash and then by exact fields; the next tier is tracked as the
feature "Recovery tier 3: rank candidates for a broken identity by similar content" (`oas-4ti`).
That whole subsystem is reachable only by notes the search FOUND. An empty field is not damage the
tool repairs — it is damage the tool cannot see.

**HOW IT WAS FOUND.** While reviewing the add-on fix for the silent Edit keypress (`oas-kxf`), a
reviewing agent traced the message that fix produces. The message told the person to re-sync, on
the reasonable assumption that a missing identity is a recoverable state — which is true for every
note the tool can see. The message was wrong, and tracing WHY it was wrong is what exposed this.

**WHY IT IS WORSE THAN AN UNCOUNTED NOTE.** `model/CardSearch.scala:29-31` states the consequence
of the search missing notes, in the repository's own words: the half it misses "looks to this tool
like notes that DO NOT EXIST — which is the input that makes it create them again. Duplicating a
collection is the worst outcome available here." If the source note is still in the vault, a run
creates a fresh Anki note while the invisible one keeps the review history.

---

**PRIORITY REFLECTS UNMEASURED INCIDENCE, NOT SEVERITY.** No instance has been confirmed in the
live collection. The class is severe; how reachable it is has not been established.

**SUGGESTIONS, not a choice. Each is separable.**

- Measure first. One search in Anki's browser answers whether any such note exists today, and the
  candidate routes to producing one are worth writing down: a note created by hand in Anki on an
  owned note type (two clicks, and the field is empty permanently); a bulk tag cleanup in the
  browser stripping the legacy tag from a note that never had the field written; an accidental
  field edit.
- Widen the enumeration so the search asks a question an empty field can answer, and decide what
  the tool then does with such a note — report it, offer it to the recovery tiers, or leave it.
- Do nothing but record the limit, if measurement shows nothing can produce one.

**RELATED.** `oas-ecu` — "a collection cannot tell one vault's cards from another's" — is the other
open bug about what this same collection-wide enumeration can and cannot distinguish. The two
should be read together before either changes that search, which is the riskiest surface in the
tool.
title: A note on an owned type with an empty identity field is invisible to the tool

39. **THE PYTHON ADD-ON'S SURFACE IS LARGER THAN IT HAS TO BE.** Measured 2026-08-29, after Marc
    asked whether Python was needed at all. **Nothing is built.**

    **Python is unavoidable** — Anki's extension mechanism is Python, and binding a key inside
    the reviewer requires an add-on. **499 production lines**: `core.py` 205 (pure, tested),
    `__init__.py` 294 (imports `aqt`, so untestable by construction).

    **IRREDUCIBLE**: hooking Anki's edit action, reading the add-on's config, opening a link,
    showing a tooltip, running a subprocess. That is the glue, and it is the part that cannot be
    unit-tested anyway.

    **REDUCIBLE, and worth naming separately.**

    - **~50 lines exist only because the tool runs on a JVM** — the `JAVA_HOME` hunt, the
      missing-Java diagnosis, the hint text. Accidental complexity from the runtime rather than
      the domain; a native binary deletes all of it.
    - **The drill's deck naming and search construction are DOMAIN LOGIC in the wrong language.**
      What a deck is called, what counts as one of ours, how a search is built — the Scala
      decides exactly these things everywhere else, and here they are re-decided in Python with
      their own reasoning written out fresh.

    **NOT reducible, and it was checked**: the wire format between the two is already good.
    `locate` puts a URI on stdout and an explanation on stderr, and `interpret` is five lines.
    Channel splitting, not prose parsing. Left alone.
